chapters.html:
Phainon and Mydeimos lived in a world where disappointment was never an option. All their lives, they had been treated less like children and more like ornaments of their household, trophies for proud parents to parade, proof of prestige and worth. Their role was simple, to give their families something to boast about.

Perhaps that was why the two of them understood each other so well. They shared the same lingering ghost, the same quiet weight on their shoulders. And in that shadow, they found it easier to carry one another’s burdens.

When things get heavy at their household, they find home in each other's presence. Sometimes home is not a place but a person, it's wherever one feels safe the most and wherever one can truly be themselves.

When Mydeimos turned twenty-five, it marked nearly two decades of him and Phainon being inseparable. In all those years, Phainon was certain he had Mydei memorized, just as Mydei surely had him. But that certainty shattered that exact night, Eurypon–Mydei’s father–lifted his glass at the dinner table and raised a toast.

“Good evening, everyone. Thank you for coming to my dear son’s birthday.” Eurypon started. He glanced at almost every soul in the dining table before settling his eyes on the man wearing a dark blue tuxedo, beside her son. Phainon politely nodded and smiled at Mydei’s father.

The dinner party held for Mydei’s birthday was dressed in formality. Though they’d been told it would be intimate, nearly every guest was a stranger, with faces they recognized only in passing through their parents’ wide-reaching circles. For Mydei, the only truly familiar presence in the room was Phainon.

Phainon's gaze reached the man beside who seemed to be having some trouble. Mydei's mother, Gorgo was sitting in front of them, her eyes followed Phainon’s every move as he leaned into Mydei’s ears, whispering something.

“You okay, Dei?” It was painfully obvious to Phainon that his friend seemed everything but fine, yet when Mydei nodded in response, he did not pry. He figured a talk after the party would make his friend feel better. Phainon sat quietly, eyes returning back to the speaker at the middle of the table, who was obviously spying their movements.

Gorgo turned to the other guests before continuing her speech.

“This toast is first and foremost to my one and only child who has brought our family pride and happiness. Mydeimos, happy birthday, my son.” A soft smile was etched on Eurypon’s lips that Mydei reciprocated, which seem geniune to everybody sitting on the table but Phainon.

Glasses clinked all over the room as soft laughter and congratulations echoed through the room. All the attention poured towards Mydei who was sitting quietly, lips sealed tightly. He looked so troubled that made Phainon's worry grow larger, his right hand slipping under the table to hold on Mydei's. Phainon felt Mydei's hands tightened against his as the crowd around them celebrated loudly.

But silence fell, shortly after Eurypon raised another toast, this time a tall man standing beside him. The man looks like he's of the same age as him and Mydei, he's familiar but Phainon couldn't pinpoint who he is exactly.

“I have another toast to make. In celebration of my son's birthday, I would like to announce our family’s engagement with my dear friend, Anthony, through our children's marriage and an heir to follow, of course.” The crowd giggled and cheered with Eurypon at his last sentiment, their voices louder this time, congratulations were in the air, but Phainon and Mydei's world seemed to have stopped.

Smiles are plastered on the lips of the guests and yet Mydei's lips have never shut as tight as before, his hands never cold as before, and when he felt the grip of Phainon's hands loosening, Mydei almost stood up from his chair.

Phainon’s mind went utterly silent. The words from Mydei’s father refused to take shape in his head, and before he realized it, his body betrayed him first, his fingers slipped from Mydei’s hand.

Across the noise of laughter and clinking glasses, their eyes found each other. In Mydei’s gaze, Phainon caught the unmistakable swell of tears. He drew breath to speak, but Mydei was already rising, his chair scraping sharply against the floor. Without a word, he strode towards the door, silence hovering over him as people's eyes followed suit.

The room stirred with whispers, a low hum that pressed in on every side. Phainon couldn’t care less. All he could do was follow, past the curious stares, out of the crowded hall, and straight to where Mydei had fled.

Phainon knocked twice before turning the door knob only for it to be locked from the other side.

“Dei.” It was soft, the softest Phainon's voice ever sounded and Mydei couldn't stop his heart from aching just by the sound of it. “Dei, open up, please.”

Phainon was almost begging and he was ready to beg harder if Mydei hadn't opened the door.

His room was almost empty, with only the necessary furnishing and some of the old things Mydei had when they were younger and was living with his parents.

Mydei sat on the edge of his bed in silence, his back on Phainon. And with the softest of touch, Phainon reached out his hands to touch Mydei's shoulders.

“Do you want to talk?” He paused for a while, reading Mydei's silence. “Honestly, I wanna ask a lot of questions, what's with the engagement? with a man? another man, and an heir? I’m so confused, but I don't wanna press you on telling something you're not comfortable to open up. But, I’m your friend and it's just… I don't know what to say, Dei.”

Phainon felt like he was tiptoeing around Mydei, not sure what words to use, what gestures to do. He remained still, sitting on his friend's side.

A long silence fell between them. Mydei couldn't bring himself to be truthful towards Phainon, he didn't mean to deceive him, but he's not really deceiving him, is he? He's not obligated to tell every single thing to Phainon, but a part inside of him felt so guilty for not telling Phainon something important about himself.

If Mydei's honest, he's scared. He's scared about what Phainon would say if he'd found out Mydei was different, would he give him a weird look? Would he see Mydei differently? Treat him differently? Would their friendship end because of it? Would… would Phainon feel disgusted?

But he realized Phainon's the only one who can answer all the questions in his head that he kept on overthinking.

“It’s what we're meant to do for our parents, isn't it? Get married to someone convenient for them, have children to continue their lineage.” Mydei let out a deep sigh, his head lowering, as if bowing to shame. “I haven't been truthful to you.”

“About what, Dei?”

Slowly, Mydei turned around, his body facing Phainon yet his head still hung low. He doesn't have the face to tell Phainon everything, the most intimate thing about him, something he never bared to anyone. Something only his parents and trusted Physichian knew.

“You see, Phai, I’m… it's different.” Mydei's voice sounded almost like a whisper.

“What's different?” And Phainon's were begging.

Phainon reached out, gently turning Mydei’s face towards him and the sight nearly stole his breath. The Mydei he knew was unshakable, never one to break, never one to shed tears, even when reduced to a mere ornament in the eyes of others, even when he spoke of his struggles. He carried sadness, yes, but he never let it spill.

Now, that strength was crumbling before him. Mydei’s eyes were red, swollen, glistening with tears he could no longer hold back. His lips were raw from biting down, a futile attempt to keep the sobs inside.

Mydei couldn’t even speak, every attempt at a sentence broke apart into a mournful sob. At his most vulnerable, Phainon became the only refuge he had, pulling him into a tight embrace, tucking him against his chest. His hand moved in slow circles along Mydei’s back, giving him comfort, and in that moment Mydei found his home again.

It was there, in the crook of Phainon’s neck, that his tear-streaked face fit so perfectly as though the creator himself had shaped them as a single figure, only torn apart by the hand of fate.

Phainon was thankful no one followed them inside, he was grateful that they respected Mydei’s boundaries and no one barged in his room to interrogate him. He could not bear to let anyone see this side of Mydei, as possessive as it sounds, he's not comfortable sharing Mydei's vulnerability to anyone, it's his to feel, for him to console.

“You don't have to say it, if you're not comfortable, Dei, it's okay.” Phainon kept on mumbling “It's okay.” as he tightened his hold onto his friend.

They stayed in the same position for a long while before Mydei broke out of his embrace, his long fingers brushing his locks and wiping his face.

With a soft and low voice, Mydeimos confessed, almost like a whisper to wind.

“Phai… I have a different organ from the usual male and I…” He was unsure how to phrase it. There was a brief pause before he continued. “I… can conceive a child, and I need to… And they expect me to marry a man my father chose for me.”

Phainon thought about all the revelation Mydei could possibly make but never this. He can conceive? A child? A real human child? By another man? Another?

The silence that fell onto them felt like minutes stretched to eternity. They remained on the same position, no one moving an inch as if they had turned into stone figures. And with each silence, Mydei’s anxiety grew even larger.

Phainon scrambled his thoughts for the proper words to say to the anxious Mydeimos but his feelings spoke faster than his rational mind.

“Why do you need other man? I’m a man too.”

Phainon was just as shocked as Mydei when he realized what he had said. But his building anxiety eased up when he heard laughter from the man beside him.

That's when he looked at Mydeimos who was laughing hard, his eyes gleaming with soft tears. Although his laughter eased Phainon, it strike a painful nail onto his heart. Mydei thinks it's a joke.

“Aren’t you a bit surprised about my revelation? Disguted even.”

Phainon's brows furrowed at Mydei's words for himself.

“Surprised, I was. But disgusted? Why would I be disgusted with you, Dei?”

“It's not normal, Phainon.”

The once soft conversation heated the next few seconds. Both their voice raising, their body rising from the bed.

“Then you're unique, you're you. What wrong about it?”

“Goodness, Phainon! Do you not know the severity of this situation? I’m basically a woman with this thing on me.”

Phainon felt helpless by the second passing. He wanted to remain calm but when even the usual stoic Mydei was fuming, he couldn't keep his head cool.

“I know, that's why I’m asking what's wrong with it? And if you're more or less a woman, what about it? Since when is being a woman considered disgusting?” Phainon paused for a moment, trying to control his emotions that keep on slipping up. He realized how important every conversation they were about to exchange right now. All the words that's gonna slip out from his mouth is either gonna make or break their relationship. “There’s nothing disgusting about you, Dei. Women are amazing and so are you. I know it's hard, I couldn't imagine how hard it is for you to be expected to carry a child in your body, I couldn't imagine how hard it was for you to live your whole life differently, and your stupid best friend doesn't have a single clue of what's going on but… Dei, don't call yourself disgusting, please.”

And yet again, Mydei broke out in a mournful sob. The cries Mydei let out shattered Phainon. His anger long forgotten as he aided on Mydei's side.

Phainon held Mydei tightly to his chest, mumbling “I’m sorry” continuously until his shoulder relaxed.

Everything after that felt like a dream to Mydei, Phainon holding him up. Helping him walk towards the door, out of their mansion. Phainon was even the one who put his seatbelt on, and drove to God knows where. Mydei’s head was floating all the time Phainon was driving, glancing at Mydei from time to time only to see him staring at the window.

None of them minded the crowd of people earlier at the mansion oggling at them, they didn't even notice Eurypon who was fuming mad when they went out of Mydei's room. Or Gorgo who was trying to get closer to his son but was stopped by his husband. Or Phainon's parents who were calling for his name in desperation.

When Mydei seemed to regain his consciousness, he was already in bed, at Phainon’s apartment, and Phainon was beside him trying to coo him to sleep.

“Sleep your worries for now, Dei. Let's face it tomorrow, I’m here.” Was all Mydei heard before his mind went blank once more succumbing to oblivion.

The next morning was quite peaceful, but the bed beside Mydeimos was already cold, hinting the empty space that Phainon left.

He closed his eyes for a moment trying to recall the chaotic night he had last night. All Mydeimos could do was heave a deep sigh and as he opened his eyes again he was met by the familiar cream colored walls.

Mydei was about to get up when the door to the bedroom opened and revealed Phainon.

“Good morning, Dei. Just woke up?”

“Yeah.”

“Good. I went out to get breakfast, come to the dining area.” There was no hint of indifference or disgust in Phainon's voice. He was just… he's Phainon, the same one whom Mydei knew for years. His way of treating Mydei did not falter to change after all the things that happened and for some reason his heart tugged at that thought.

Mydei could only muster a small smile before rising from the bed and going straight to the bathroom. Phainon's stares bore holes onto Mydei's back as he strode towards the room yet Mydei feigned ignorance.

It was only inside the bathroom, under the cold shower that Mydei was able to let out a deep sigh. His mind spiralled with thoughts of the events that unfolded last night as he felt the cold water sipped through every crevice of his body.

Amidst the chaos in his mind, he weirdly felt like there's a huge weight that was lifted from his chest. At least, Phainon knows now and he doesn't seem to think differently about me. As they said, every cloud has a silver lining.

Mydeimos knew his father would one day do such a thing; deciding for his child as if he held Mydei’s life on a leash was always an easy thing for his so-called father. But he never thought it was gonna be this severe. Afterall, he hated it when any man would so much as touch his son, thinking of nothing but the worst thing that may happen between Mydei and another man. Hence why his father was disapproving of his relationship with Phainon from the very beginning.

His mother, Gorgo, would tell him that it was because his father was worried about him. But he knew better, and it's because his father is ashamed of what his son actually is, afraid that Mydeimo’s misconduct– being Mydei exploring his sexuality– would reflect on him.

But now, he even wants Mydei to marry a man, no less. It's absurd, it's the most absurd thing his father has ever done to him. He could tolerate all his father's actions before, but this is where he drew the lines. Because if he doesn't, this is gonna ruin him for good.

All those thoughts inside his head, Mydei did not realized how long he's been standing still under the shower, or how the constant banging of the bathroom door stopped together with the loud “Mydei, are you okay?!”

When reality hit him, it was already too late because the door already opened, revealing a panting Phainon, holding a key to his right hand and his heart to his left. And it seemed Phainon had a way faster reaction time than Mydei, because before he could even protest, Phainon had already screamed “I’m sorry!”, bolting out the bathroom, and yet he never forgot to close the door when he left.

Mydei was left inside, mouth agape, still processing what had actually unfolded in front of him. It was a great wake up call, because what the fuck is that?

It took him one fifth of the time he spent inside thinking, when he actually took a proper bath. Finishing only for a few minutes before he's draping the towel on his lower body.

Mydei nonchalantly went outside, with only the towel on his lower body covering him, seemingly unaware that Phainon is hanging on for his dear life and Mydei only made it worse when emerge from the bathroom looking like that. Water droplets dripping from his head down to his toned abdominal muscles, and as shameless as it is, Phainon is only a man. A man who is easily drawn to temptation– that is his best friend, roaming inside his apartment practically naked.

“Eyes up here, Phai.”

“My eyes are up there.”

“Yeah yeah… Where's my clothes?”

Phainon quickly pointed to the stack of clothes on top of his bed. When Mydei approached it, it was his cue to leave the room and go to the kitchen. He left to give Mydei privacy and ultimately to block off any unholy thoughts that were about to sip in. It is not appropriate to think such things about his friend, who is having a hard time right now and even if he's not having a hard time, it will never be appropriate.

Phainon shook his head, and grabbed a glass to drink a cup of water, hoping it washes away any thoughts he had and he might have.

It wasn't long after that when Mydei came into the kitchen, asking for the breakfast Phainon promised about. They sat down facing each other on the small corner of Phainon’s kitchen, shared a breakfast together like they used to when they were still in the college dorms. They spoke of anything in their mind, light conversations that eases their mind from the chaos that none of them predicted was approaching the same day.

Shortly after their breakfast, Phainon’s phone rang, it seemed like an important work call so he excused himself and went to the living room. It's inevitable, especially when it's a Monday morning and both of them are supposed to be at work. Mydei felt a bit guilty but he is thankful for Phainon, he needed someone to be by his side right now.

He remained sitting on the dining table, sipping on his warm cup of coffee. He thought of opening his phone, he probably has a lot of missed calls and texts from his secretary but he couldn’t make himself take a single look. Afraid that his mother might call, and she's someone he could never ignore. But he's not ready right now, he'll face her and he'll come back and fix the problem but not right now. He needed space even just for today.

He didn't realize he was lost in thoughts until Phainon came back with an irritated expression.

“What is it?”

“Hyacine called.”

“Hmm?”

“There's an emergency at work.”

“Then you should go.”

“But you're here.”

“It's an urgent matter, right?”

“You're an urgent matter too.”

Mydei couldn't help but chuckle. And he couldn't help it when his chuckle turned into full on laughter when Phainon pouted, looking at Mydei with pitiful eyes.

“Stop laughing, Dei.”

“I’m serious, tend to your work first. Finish it up then come back here, I’ll stay. I don't have anywhere else to go, anyway.”

“Are you gonna be okay here alone?”

“I will. I needed time to think anyway.”

Phainon let out a defeated sigh. Before muttering a heavy “Fine!” as he stood up to dress for work. It took him a few minutes to fully prepare, and went to Mydei who was sitting on the couch, as he was leaving.

“Call me if you need anything, Dei. If you don't wanna turn on your phone, the landline then. My number’s on the fridge if you don’t remember it.”

Phainon had another batch of reminders after that and all Mydei could do was nod his head and say “Okay.”. It took Phainon longer to remind Mydei of everything than to get ready for work. And when he left, Mydei sighed.

The apartment was suddenly so empty with just him so he turned on the TV for background noise. He roamed around Phainon's place, he's been here as many times as he did on his own place but he's trying to entertain himself by rummaging through everything inside.

When Mydei reaches the bookshelf, his fingers automatically slide through the books that's neatly tucked. It was clean, no trace of dust but Mydei is a hundred percent sure Phainon has never touched any of these, more so read any of the books. Because these books are all Mydei’s favourites. Between the two of them, it was Mydei who is the actual bookworm. He particularly likes fictional books, takes his mind out of his bitter reality. 

For some reason, everytime Mydei would narrate a book he's read to Phainon, it would end up on this bookshelf the next day and when he'd ask if Phainon has read it, he would always say that he liked to hear the plot from Mydei better than read it from the books. Which made Mydei wonder why Phainon would even purchase the physical copies in the first place. He shook his head, a small smile creeping on the side of his lips. He certainly knew why.

His slender fingers stopped to an unfamiliar book on the shelf— no, it wasn't a book. It looks like a journal, an old one, and he's never seen it before. He knew better than to pry on someone's personal life, but his curiosity took the better of him. At the back of his mind, he thought Phainon would not get mad at him for looking through some of his things.

He thought it was some kind of rubbish full of doodles and whatnots, given Phainon, but to his surprise it had actual words written inside and the penmanship was quite good.

His eyebrows shot up when he read the date, it was written when they were fourteen or so, and if his eyebrows could shoot higher, it probably would when he read the first words.

To Mydeimos.

In an instant, Mydei closed the journal. His heartbeat is racing and is about to burst out of his chest. He had a thought, he saw the hints, he wasn't born yesterday, but he denied all his thoughts ever since they were but young boys.

To read Phainon's journal, his letter to Mydei, is to acknowledge the truth that Mydei had been brushing off since time immemorial. There was an unusual fear that crept into his mind, his rational thoughts screaming not to look any further but his curiosity is winning against him.

He could not help but open the journal again and read the letters until the very end. The journal had more than a hundred pages and all of it was filled up by hand written letters from Phainon. All were addressed to a single person, Mydeimos.

The very last letter in the journal was one written today, and all there's left in the journal was 3 pages of blank paper. But that's a less important detail compared to the contents of the letters. 

There's over a hundred letters but Mydei can summarize the content in a few words. They were all letters written to confess Phainon's feelings towards his best friend for nearly two decades. And in all letters there is one phrase that Phainon would always write at the end.

In a field of ten thousand stars, my eyes would always find your light, Mydeimos.

Mydeimos didn't realize the tears streaming down his face as he finished the letters, he was sitting on the cold floor, his back on the shelf. He’s crying, but there wasn't a hint of single sadness in his heart. He felt full, he felt weird but he didn't feel any remorse, ultimately, he felt loved.

And it was something Phainon had never failed to make him feel ever since they were kids, whether as friends or as something more.

Mydei would lie if he'd say he didn't know that there was always something more to the way Phainon looks at him, he's quick witted and Phainon wears his heart on his sleeves. But it was the friendship that Mydei was trying to save that is holding him back from acknowledging Phainon's feelings. 

Phainon is someone he would love to keep by his side until they're both old and gray, and he thought that keeping him as his friend is what will keep him by his side longer. Especially given the circumstances Mydei is in, he has always been afraid of Phainon finding out his secret even if almost all the people around them knew about it. Mydei was way more shocked when he found out Phainon knew nothing about it— or maybe he does. Maybe he heard rumors but it's Phainon, he's never one to believe rumors about his beloved friend if it didn't come from him directly, and he's never one to press Mydei on telling him something he's not ready to say.

Mydei closed his eyes tight and a soft chuckle left his mouth.

“Oh, Phainon. Come home, faster.”

But it wasn't Phainon who came home first.

Mydei fell asleep in the bedroom holding the journal in his chest and when he was woken up by the sudden loud ringing from the intercom. Someone was outside and it's definitely not the person Mydei was waiting for.

He quickly got up and attended to the door when he saw who was outside. It was Gorgo and Eurypon. His footsteps halted and his hands trembled, he never expected his parents, especially his father to be the one to reach out first after the incident and he'd be lying if he said he's not afraid.

Eurypon scared him, and it's even unimaginably scary thinking about his unpredictable action. What will he do to me if I open the door? What will he do to Phainon?

He made up his mind on not letting them in but when he saw his crying mother, trying to step his father to ring the doorbell any farther and even begged his father to just go back home, his heart melted. He couldn't help but open the door for his mother who attacked him with a tight hug the moment he saw his dear son.

The old lady cried his heart out on her son’s chest, mumbling “I’m sorry”. But as soon as her mother let him go, he received a slap from his father whose eyes were almost red from anger.

“Eurypon! What are you doing?!” Gorgo doesn't know what to do. Stop his husband or aid his son who was taken aback from the sudden abuse.

“What am I doing? I’m teaching this bastard about discipline. Where is he, huh? Where is that other bastard of yours? Tell me and I will slap that mother fucker a thousand times harder than I did you!” He was in rage. His emotions take the better of him and Mydei doesn't know what to do.

Eurypon was strict but he was never abusive, at least, physically. It was the first time in his twenty-five years that someone slapped him, and it's his father who did so.

Despite how big Mydei is, his trauma and his fear are larger than his body. It froze his entire system, rendering him unable to even speak and answer his father.

It was chaos. Eurypon uttered a lot of words that Mydei wasn't able to register in his mind as he stood there, in the living room, holding his left cheek. His mother was crying and begging his father to stop his madness but who can stop a mad man? Not even his wife could.

And it was that scene that Phainon came home too. His scream thundered through the room that even Eurypon was silenced.

“What the fuck is happening here?!”

Phainon rushed on Mydei’s side, his deadly stare could kill the mad man standing in front of them but Eurypon fought an equal death match.

“You're finally home? Is there where you screw my son, huh? Where he whores himself out to you? You fucking disgusting–”, he couldn't even finish his sentence when a fist landed on his face. 

“Don't you dare talk shit about your son. I want to respect you as his father but don't  you ever dare put your hands on Mydeimos in my own house.” Phainon's voice was firm, laced with nothing but anger.

But even when Eurypon’s face was aching, he didn't stop from his fit of rage.

“You fucking disrespectful child. Mydeimos? Is this the man you're whoring yourself to? Huh?! You ungrateful bastard! I gave everything to you, I clothed you, I fed you, I gave you all the things you could ever want and all I expect is for a disgusting bastard like you to use your freakiness to pay me back. Is it hard to marry Charles? Huh?! You bitch? You like to get fucked by men, anyway. Now I’m giving you something you want, yet you've embarrassed me in front of everyone?!” 

Eurypon was livid and so was everyone else. Mydei held Phainon from punching his father one more time, but he couldn't hold back his mother from slapping the shit out of him.

With tears streaming down Gorgo’s face, her mouth spouts a series of profanities that Mydei never imagined his mother could do. The most gentle woman he's ever seen in his life was like an enraged tiger.

The room was filled with shouting and chaos when Mydei finally spoke.

“I couldn't do it anyway.”

“What?” The room grew silent, waiting for Mydei’s next words.

“I can't marry anyone anyway. I’m pregnant.” If there was a next level to the silence before, that was it. As if everyone's been freezed even with their breathings. Not a single person moved an inch, when he spoke again. “Phainon and I are expecting.”

It was Phainon who reacted first. “What?”
